For those I haven’t met, I’m Mia, Hannah’s best friend and very proud maid of honor.

Hannah has given me two important jobs today: keep track of her bouquet and give a speech without embarrassing her. The bouquet is doing beautifully. We’ll see how the rest goes.

Being Hannah’s best friend means having someone who celebrates your good news like it’s her own, answers the phone when you’ve had a terrible day, and tells you honestly when an outfit isn’t working—although usually after asking, “How attached are you to it?”

One of my favorite memories of Hannah is from a night when I’d had a truly awful week. She came over with snacks and promised we didn’t have to talk about it. We could just watch a movie.

Naturally, we talked through the entire movie.

To this day, neither of us knows how it ends. But I remember how much better I felt when she left. That’s Hannah. She shows up, makes room for whatever you’re feeling, and somehow gets you laughing before the evening is over.

So when she started telling me about Andrew, I paid attention.

At first, I got the usual details: he was kind, he was funny, and she really liked spending time with him. Then his name began appearing in almost every conversation.

“How was your weekend?”
“Andrew and I—”

“Have you tried that new restaurant?”
“Actually, Andrew—”

“What’s the weather like?”
“Well, Andrew thinks—”

I had a suspicion.

But what convinced me wasn’t how often she talked about him. It was seeing them together. Hannah could be completely herself with Andrew: silly, thoughtful, excited, occasionally very certain that her directions were better than the navigation.

And Andrew looked delighted to be there. Even during the directions.

Andrew, what means the most to me is the way you pay attention to her. You listen to her stories. You appreciate her humor. You notice when she needs a little encouragement or someone to sit beside her. As her best friend, it’s a wonderful thing to see her so loved—and to see how much she loves you.

I’m also grateful that you’ve welcomed me into your life, because Hannah and I do have a longstanding agreement involving frequent phone calls and conversations that begin with, “Quick question,” and last forty-five minutes. Thank you for your understanding.

Hannah, we’ve shared so many ordinary days that became favorite memories simply because we were together. Getting to stand beside you on this extraordinary day means more than I can say. You look beautiful, you seem so happy, and I’m trying very hard to make it through this paragraph without needing the emergency tissues.

You and Andrew have so much ahead of you: adventures, milestones, quiet evenings, and probably a lengthy discussion about what to have for dinner. I hope you keep enjoying each other through all of it. Keep being curious about each other. Keep making each other laugh. And when one of you has had an awful week, I hope there are always snacks and a movie you never quite finish.

Everyone, please raise your glass.

To Hannah and Andrew: may your home be full of warmth, your lives full of friendship, and your marriage full of moments you can’t wait to tell each other about.

I love you both. Cheers!"}
